description.en-US: The order this line belongs to. Immutable: moving a line between orders would change two orders' totals at once, and the one it left would keep a total it can no longer justify.

Position within the order, unique per order. It is a stable identifier and not merely display order: a return names the line it returns, and a fiscal document lists lines by number, so renumbering an existing line would repoint documents already issued. Starts at 1 rather than 0 because it appears on customer-facing paperwork.

What kind of thing this line is. A product line sells one variant. A combo line is the virtual parent of a bundle whose real variants live in sales_order_line_components, because Inventory fulfils real variants and never a virtual combo (BR 17). A promotion_reward line is a free item given by a promotion, which is a real line rather than an adjustment because Inventory must physically fulfil it and its VAT treatment is a line-level question (D-11). The fields each type requires are enforced by the domain service, not by required_for_create, because the schema cannot express a requirement conditional on another field.

What is being sold. The variant, not the template: the variant is the transactable unit. Nullable because a combo parent line sells no single variant — its components do. Required for product and promotion_reward lines, enforced by the domain service. A plain ulid, since the product belongs to Inventory.

The product's code AS IT WAS when the sale happened. A snapshot rather than a join, and that is the whole point of the field: a product renamed or recoded next year must not silently change what a receipt issued today says was sold. Immutable after confirm (BR 11), enforced by the domain service.
The product's name as it appeared on the receipt. Snapshot for the same reason as the code, and it is the field a customer will quote back in a support conversation. Immutable after confirm.

The unit the quantities on this line are expressed in. Required on every line: a quantity without its unit is not a quantity. Sales registers a UomUsageProbe so that Essential refuses to change a unit's factor while sales history references it (BR-UOM-ESS-020) — without the probe, editing a unit would reinterpret quantities already sold.

How much the customer bought, in uom_id. Must be strictly greater than zero — a line ordering nothing is not a line — which the domain service enforces, because the framework declares no CHECK constraints and a min of 0 cannot express 'greater than'. Scale 6 rather than the monetary 4: a quantity can legitimately be a fraction of a unit in a way money cannot.

Whether this line owes physical goods. False for a service, a fee or a non-stocked item, which is what makes an order of only such lines reach fulfillment_status 'not_required' rather than sitting pending forever (D-14). Defaults to TRUE, deliberately: a line wrongly marked as needing goods holds an order open until somebody notices, while one wrongly marked as needing none reports a sale as complete that never shipped. Whether a variant is actually stock-managed is Inventory's judgement and arrives with SALES-048's product port; until then every line takes the default.

How much has actually been handed over. Separate from ordered_quantity because partial fulfilment is normal (BR 87.8): a kiosk dispenses two of three items and the third jams. Must never exceed ordered_quantity — the invariant of BR 55, enforced in the domain service.

How much has come back. The ceiling depends on whether the line ever owed physical goods (D-32, confirmed 28/08/2026): for goods that ship it is fulfilled_quantity, since a customer cannot return what was never handed over; for a service or any non-stocked line it is ordered_quantity instead, because there was no delivery step and measuring against one would make such lines permanently un-refundable - which BR 52 forbids, requiring refund without physical return to be possible. See ReturnableQuantity in domain/services/return_states.go, which is the single implementation of that rule.

The catalogue or pricelist price before anything was applied. Kept alongside the effective price so that a receipt can show what the customer would have paid, and so the price explanation API can start from the number the discount chain began with.

The per-unit price actually charged, after price-level rules. Zero on a promotion_reward line, which is exactly what makes a free item expressible as a real line rather than as a discount that would have to be allocated back somewhere.

effective_unit_price times ordered_quantity, before line discounts. Stored rather than recomputed on read: the multiplication is rounded once, here, and every downstream total must agree with that one rounding rather than repeat it and possibly differ.

Everything taken off this line, as a POSITIVE number — including this line's share of an order-level discount, allocated by the pricing engine. Positive for the same reason discount_total is on the order: a report of discount given should not have to flip a sign.

gross_amount minus discount_amount: the taxable base for this line. The sum of every line's net_amount is what an order-level allocation must add back up to exactly, which is why the residual of a proportional split is assigned deterministically rather than left to rounding (D-04).

The tax rate applied, as a FRACTION, AS IT WAS at the time of sale: 0.1 for 10%. Note the unit — accounting stores a rate as a percentage, and the conversion happens once, at the boundary in services.ResolveBasketTax. Snapshotted rather than looked up, so that a later rate change cannot reinterpret a historical sale. For a line carrying several taxes this is their sum, enough to read the line at a glance; the exact per-tax figures live in the order's tax_snapshot.

The tax on this line's net amount, as the accounting module computed it. The base is the line's NET — gross less every discount and promotion — because Sales owns discount logic and passes the post-discount base (BR-TAX-ESS-026); taxing the gross would charge the customer on money they never paid.
What this line contributes to the grand total: net_amount plus tax_amount. Stored so that the order total is the sum of stored line numbers rather than a re-derivation that could round differently.

Where this line's price came from. It is what lets the price-explanation API answer 'why does this cost this' without replaying the whole engine, and what makes a manual override visible as a deliberate act rather than as an unexplained number.

The promotion that created this line, set on promotion_reward lines (D-11). Nullable everywhere else. It is what makes a free item traceable to the campaign that gave it away, which is the question asked when a campaign's cost is reviewed.

The combo definition this line instantiates, set on combo parent lines. Nullable elsewhere. A plain ulid rather than an edge: the combo may be archived or redefined after the sale, and the line must keep meaning what it meant without depending on the definition still existing in its original form.
